name: Impeccable
tagline: Design skill for AI coding agents: 23 slash commands and 59 detector rules
description: Impeccable is a design-guidance skill that installs into an AI coding harness and gives it a shared design vocabulary. It ships one skill with 23 slash commands (init, craft, shape, critique, audit, polish, bolder, quieter, distill, harden, onboard, animate, colorize, typeset, layout, delight, overdrive, clarify, adapt, optimize, live, document, extract) plus 59 deterministic detector rules that flag AI design tells such as Inter-for-everything, purple-to-blue gradients, cards nested in cards, gray text on colored backgrounds and bounce easing. `/impeccable init` writes PRODUCT.md and DESIGN.md so every later command reads the same project context. It targets developers who let an agent build the frontend and want the output to stop looking machine-made.
pricing_detail: Skill, CLI and Chrome extension are free and Apache-2.0. The impeccable.style site markets a Pro tier for the 'design worlds' deck (177 worlds, growing weekly); no public price listed.
agent_guidance: Install this at project start, before any UI exists: run `npx impeccable install` then `/impeccable init` so PRODUCT.md and DESIGN.md exist for every later command to read. It is the strongest general-purpose replacement for Anthropic's frontend-design skill and it composes with a brand-specific DESIGN.md from awesome-design-md or hue - Impeccable supplies craft rules, the DESIGN.md supplies the visual identity. Watch out that it ships no components and no code: it will not build a design system for you, it critiques and reshapes what you already generated, and the 59 detector rules run deterministically via `npx impeccable detect src/` with no LLM, so use that in CI rather than burning tokens on a critique pass.
why_it_matters: It is the most-adopted design skill for AI coding harnesses and the clearest codification of what AI-generated UI gets wrong, expressed as rules an agent can actually execute.

name: getdesign.md
tagline: Browsable catalog of DESIGN.md brand analyses for AI coding agents
description: getdesign.md is the web front end for the DESIGN.md collection maintained by the VoltAgent team. Each entry is a plain-markdown analysis of a real brand's visual language - colors and their roles, typography rules, component styling, layout, elevation, responsive behaviour, do's and don'ts, and an agent prompt guide - that you paste into a project so a coding agent builds pages in that style. 75 brands are listed on the homepage, from Linear, Stripe, Vercel and Claude to Ferrari, Nike and a 1996 Dell revival; the site markets a larger 300+ catalog. Free browsing sits alongside a paid Catalog Pass and a Website Starter Kit.

name: Awesome DESIGN.md
tagline: 73 MIT-licensed DESIGN.md brand analyses you drop into a project root
description: A curated GitHub collection of DESIGN.md files - the plain-text design-system document introduced by Google Stitch - covering 73 listed brands across ten categories: AI and LLM platforms, developer tools, backend and DevOps, productivity SaaS, design and creative tools, fintech and crypto, e-commerce, media and consumer tech, automotive, and a retro-web nostalgia set. Each folder holds a DESIGN.md with nine sections (visual theme, color palette and roles, typography rules, component stylings, layout principles, depth and elevation, do's and don'ts, responsive behaviour, agent prompt guide) plus preview.html and preview-dark.html renderings. You copy one file into your project root and tell the agent to follow it. This is the free MIT mirror of the getdesign.md catalog.

name: hue
tagline: Agent skill that turns any brand URL or screenshot into a design system
description: hue is an MIT-licensed skill for Claude Code and Codex that reads a brand from a URL, a name, or a screenshot and writes out a complete design language as a second, generated skill: color tokens, typography, spacing, light and dark mode, hero-stage recipes, icon-kit selection, and a component library. You clone it into ~/.claude/skills or ~/.agents/skills once, then say 'make a design skill from cursor.com' in any session. Every generated skill is gated through scripts/validate.mjs, which checks YAML syntax, orphan CSS selectors, undefined var(--token) usages, leftover placeholders, em-dashes, the SKILL.md frontmatter contract, WCAG contrast on core text/background pairs, and AI-default display fonts. Seventeen worked examples ship in examples/, each with design-model.yaml and landing-page.html.

agent_guidance: Reach for hue when the target brand is NOT in awesome-design-md's 73 and you need a system invented from a URL or screenshot - it is a generator, where DESIGN.md collections are a lookup. Install path matters: ~/.claude/skills/hue for Claude Code, ~/.agents/skills/hue (or $CODEX_HOME/skills/hue) for Codex, and after generating always run `node scripts/validate.mjs <generated-skill-folder>` because it exits 1 on undefined var(--token) usages and failed WCAG contrast, which is the single most common way a generated system silently breaks. It composes cleanly with Impeccable - hue defines the identity, Impeccable enforces craft - but note the output is vanilla CSS custom properties and HTML, not React or Tailwind, so you translate before dropping it into a component framework.
why_it_matters: Most design-for-agents tooling hands you a fixed style; hue is one of the few that derives a validated, self-consistent system from an arbitrary brand and then hard-fails on its own mistakes.
notable_for: generates a skill from a URL or screenshot
validate.mjs gates WCAG contrast and orphan tokens
works on Claude Code and Codex

name: hue (hueapp.io)
tagline: Landing site and live demo for the hue design-system skill
description: hueapp.io is the public site for hue, the open-source Claude Code and Codex skill that turns a brand URL or screenshot into a design system. It explains the flow, shows the eight files a generated skill produces, and hosts a browsable rendering of the output - 95 tokens, 40 components with 156 variants, light and dark mode. It is a showcase and entry point, not a separate product: the installable artifact is the GitHub repo it links to. Free, no account and no API key.
pricing_detail: Free. No account, no API key. Optional sponsorship of the author.
agent_guidance: Send a human here to see what hue's output looks like before committing; do not send an agent here to install anything - clone github.com/dominikmartn/hue into the skills directory instead. The one thing this URL gives you that the repo does not is the rendered component library, useful for confirming the 40-component / 156-variant surface area and the dark-light pairing before you generate a system. Treat this and the hue repo entry as one product with two front doors.
why_it_matters: It is the proof-of-output for hue - the rendered library is what convinces a team that an agent-generated design system is actually coherent.
notable_for: rendered demo of a hue-generated system
marketing front door for the GitHub skill

name: Claude Design 2-Hour Course
tagline: 118-minute walkthrough: brand to design system to shipped site with Claude Design
description: A free two-hour YouTube masterclass by Nate Herk on Anthropic's Claude Design tool. It builds a fictional brand called Tally end to end - design system, pitch deck, landing-page wireframes, high-fidelity website, mobile app prototype, and a launch video - then deploys the site to GitHub and Vercel through Claude Code, and closes with tactics for stretching session limits. Chaptered across 13 timestamps, roughly 201k views as of August 2026. It is a screen-recorded workflow tutorial, and it funnels toward the author's free Skool community and paid course.
pricing_detail: Video is free. Upsells: free Skool 'AI Automation Society' group and a paid 'AI Automation Society Plus' membership; affiliate links for Glaido and Hostinger VPS.
agent_guidance: This is human-only material - there is no transcript endpoint, no code repo, and nothing here an agent can consume, so never cite it as a technical source. Point a user at it when they have never opened Claude Design and want to watch the whole arc once (chapters at 11:33 design system, 40:45 hi-fi website, 57:51 mobile prototype, 1:42:01 GitHub and Vercel deploy). Be aware it is a creator-funnel video: the workflow is real, the recommendations around it are sponsored, and its 'stretching your session limit' segment describes 2026 plan behaviour that will drift.
why_it_matters: It is the most-watched end-to-end demonstration of Claude Design as an actual production workflow rather than a feature tour.
notable_for: builds one brand end to end
covers GitHub + Vercel deploy via Claude Code
